copy.headline: Government plans to cut early pension for worn-out workers

extended.text: The government wants to cut seniorpension, Denmark's early pension for worn-out workers, saving 200 million kroner in 2028 and 800 million kroner in 2030, according to the Finance Ministry. The change is in the finance bill for 2027, which Peter Hummelgaard, the finance minister, presents on Friday. Jyllands-Posten has seen the bill.
Today people qualify six years before the state pension age if they can work at most 15 hours a week in their latest job. Under the plan, their capacity would be judged against any job.
Every party behind the 2019 scheme must agree for the change to take effect before an election, Jyllands-Posten writes. Dansk Folkeparti, a nationalist party and one of them, refuses.
The Arne pension, a right to retire early after a set number of years in work, would rise by about 3,000 kroner a month from its maximum of 15,650 kroner.

Unions for childcare workers, nurses and university graduates object. Dorthe Boe Danbjørg, who chairs Dansk Sygeplejeråd, the nurses' union, calls the plan 'deeply unfair'. Søren Kryhlmand of Dansk Industri, an employers' organisation, calls it 'a really good step'.

copy.headline: Hacker says Denmark's civil register was breached with the password '123456'

standard.text: An anonymous hacker who claims to have taken 8,749,975 records from the CPR register, Denmark's civil registration system, told Politiken the password was '123456'.
It was the leaked password of a former employee at a small company with access to the register. The hacker says the break-in was on 11 September and there are no plans to sell or leak the records.
Emil Hørning, a security expert at the firm Defend Denmark, examined the file for Politiken and thinks the account is probably true.
Christina Egelund, the digitalisation minister, admits in writing that security was not good enough, says that way in is now closed and has asked for a security review.

copy.headline: Immigration dominates Denmark's opening parliamentary debate

standard.text: Immigration policy filled much of Thursday's opening debate in the Folketing, Denmark's parliament, which ran for 16 hours.
Mette Frederiksen, leader of the Social Democrats, said of certain Muslims: 'I wish they were not here.'

The centre-right opposition attacked the government's plan to grant citizenship to 2,000 foreigners before applicants are screened for anti-democratic views. Anders Vistisen of Dansk Folkeparti, a nationalist party, said that risked making Islamist extremists Danish citizens. Rasmus Stoklund, the Social Democrats' political spokesman, replied that Venstre, a liberal party, had welcomed the 2,000 in January, when it was in government.

copy.headline: Venstre sinks to 5.8 per cent, its lowest poll ever

standard.text: Venstre, a liberal party, stands at 5.8 per cent in a poll by Epinion, a polling firm, for DR published on Thursday. The party has never polled lower.

Five of its MPs, Søren Gade among them, voted against the party line on a law tightening farmers' use of fertiliser. On Tuesday Gade said he might again vote 'by his own conviction' on a proposed national pesticide ban.

Søs Marie Serup, the party's former press chief, blames conflicts over farming and climate that built up over a long time, not Troels Lund Poulsen, the party leader. 'This term will be like walking through hell,' she told Kristeligt Dagblad.

copy.headline: University of Copenhagen will merge its theology faculty into humanities after 549 years

standard.text: The University of Copenhagen will merge its Faculty of Theology, one of the four faculties it was founded with in 1479, into a joint Faculty of Humanities and Theology on 1 January 2028. Law and social sciences will merge on the same day. In 2029 the health and science faculties will each split in two, which leaves the university with six faculties.

The university says most students will notice nothing, because programmes will not change. David Dreyer Lassen, the rector, says in a statement that the faculties have grown very unequal in size and complexity, which strains the university's leadership.
Martin Ravn, a theologian and parish priest, told Kristeligt Dagblad the restructuring made him 'worried about theology's future as a university subject'.

short.text: The University of Copenhagen will merge its Faculty of Theology, one of its four original faculties from 1479, into a joint Faculty of Humanities and Theology on 1 January 2028. The university says programmes will not change.

copy.deck: Law and social sciences will merge too in 2028; two other faculties split in 2029, leaving six.
